comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/limerickforyoursprog this post needs more detail on how you used AI in development. Saying you used AI isn't the same as explaining how. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process. We're trying to keep "check out my game" posts from taking over the sub. If you don't update, this may be removed.

comments.author: limerickforyoursprog
comments.body:
I ran the rules and art style of an old board game my mentor and I had created into Claude and then finetuned it into a single-player roguelike with 10 levels. The art was then mostly re-done by Claude in its own style, as I didn't have enough art for every piece. My mentor's art was much better and had more personality, I honestly don't think genuinely talented visual artists have much to worry about, but it copied roughly where the eyes should go and some of the visual gags (the Xoldier wearing two army helmets, one on each end for example). This is a playable demo but the final version would use real art and probably use Claude to animate them attacking and dying. The puzzle mode that you can play from the menu was entirely Claude-designed and it shows because they're... fine. I got lazy for that, it's an afterthought, and for a full version I would design the puzzle mode myself. I find the core gameplay loop very fun but ALMOST all the game design was figured out before the AI coding process. I also got lazy with some of the text: this is a massive mistake we all make, along with common UI and wordiness issues, which the demo still has to an extent. The AI units Dr. X and the AI ability that lets you start with 3 extra Toekens were suggested by Claude, but they're among my least favourite options to pick and I'd rather replace them some day. I find the best way to vibecode is to write out as much as possible on paper and playtest in physical space before you start coding, lest you get sidetracked with some clanker nonsense.

What I linger on with this project is it feels like a bit of a bastardization of the original concept, a physical board game you play with friends, with human art from my mentor. On one hand, it would exist in no form at all without Claude. On the other, maybe it's better that way? I don't know, this all feels like staring into an abyss sometimes.
